Edges offered: | edge | |---| | err:loop_control->WrongIterationCount | wrong rule: Updates the loop counter so that the loop runs the wrong number of times. | right rule: The init, test and update together decide the number of passes; trace them to check the count. | | mis:loop_control->DoubleLoopIndexCount | wrong rule: for (double x = 0.0; x <= 1.0; x += 0.1) runs exactly 11 times. | right rule: Using a double as a for-loop index is legal but bad practice: the number of iterations depends on an equality test between double values, which may not give the result you expect. | | mis:loop_control->ForLoopPartSkipped | wrong rule: A pass of a loop may leave out one of its parts (the condition test, the body, the update, or the initialization). | right rule: Each pass of a for loop runs test, then body, then update, every time; the initialization runs once, at the start. | | mis:loop_control->ForUpdateBeforeBody | wrong rule: The update part of a for header (e.g. i = i - 4) runs before the body on each pass, so the first pass already sees the updated value. | right rule: The update runs after the body, before the next condition test; the first pass uses the initial value. | | mis:loop_control->IdiomOverridesCode | wrong rule: An array loop processes the whole array from index 0 to length-1 and increments its index at the end of the body, whatever the code says. | right rule: The loop visits exactly the indices that its initialisation, guard and update produce, in the order in which its statements are written. | | mis:loop_control->InfiniteLoopUnnoticed | wrong rule: A while loop always stops on its own, even if nothing in its body can make the condition false. | right rule: A while loop stops only when its condition is false at a check, so if no pass changes the variables in the condition, it never stops. | | mis:loop_control->LoopHeaderIsEquations | wrong rule: The initialization, condition and update of a for header are equations that all hold at the same time. | right rule: The three header parts are statements run at different moments: init once, then condition test, body, update, repeated. | | mis:loop_control->LoopStepAlwaysOne | wrong rule: A loop variable always goes up or down by 1, whatever the update says (so i = i - 4 is read as i--). | right rule: The loop variable changes exactly as the update expression says (i += 2, i = i - 4, i *= 2, ...). | | mis:loop_control->LoopUpdateChangesDirection | wrong rule: The update of the loop variable can change from pass to pass (e.g. switch direction) although the code is the same. | right rule: The update expression is the same on every pass; the loop variable changes by the rule written in the update. | | mis:loop_control->OffByOneBound | wrong rule: i < n and i <= n mean the same, so the loop runs until i equals n and the last pass can use a[n]. | right rule: for (i = 0; i < n; i++) runs n times with i going up to n - 1; with <= it runs n + 1 times and reaches i = n. | | mis:loop_control->PreIncrementBeforeLoop | wrong rule: With ++i in the update of for (int i = s; i < n; ++i), i is increased before the body runs, so the first pass uses s + 1. | right rule: The update runs after each pass of the body, so with either ++i or i++ the first pass uses i = s. |

(here mixing in: "++i in the for-update runs before the body each pass") | | lvl:loop_control@L1#0 | level L1 way names_the_element: Loop control is the init / continuation condition / increment scheme on an index variable that decides how many passes a loop makes and with which values. | | lvl:loop_control@L1#1 | level L1 way states_the_rule: Initialize an index variable, test a loop-continuation condition on it before each pass, and increment it as the last action of each pass; for (; ; ) packages the three. Choosing the loop: for when the passes are counted by an index, while when the loop runs until a condition changes, do-while when the body must run at least once; any one can be rewritten as another, so choose the clearest. | | lvl:loop_control@L2#0 | level L2 way line_by_line_trace: init (once) -> test -> body -> update -> test -> body -> update ... -> test false -> exit. | | lvl:loop_control@L2#1 | level L2 way output_prediction: The number of passes and the values seen follow from the three parts: for (int i = 0; i <= N; i++) makes N+1 passes with i = 0..N; with i < N it makes N passes; i += 2 visits every second value. | | lvl:loop_control@L2#2 | level L2 way one_step_execution: One update changes only the loop variable, by exactly the rule written (i++ adds 1, i = i - 4 subtracts 4); one test reads it and returns true or false without changing it. | | lvl:loop_control@L3#0 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: All three control parts act on the loop variable: the init sets it, the condition tests it, the update changes it. | | lvl:loop_control@L3#1 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: The for header is exactly the three control slots, separated by semicolons; the body runs after the test and before the update. | | lvl:loop_control@L3#2 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: The update i = i + 1 is usually written i++ (or i += k for other steps); as a whole update statement ++i and i++ are equivalent. | | lvl:loop_control@L3#3 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: A loop is infinite when the update never moves the variable toward making the condition false (e.g. condition i > 3 with update i = i + 1). | | lvl:loop_control@L3#4 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: The continuation condition fixes the number of iterations, so a sharper bound (i <= n/i instead of i < n) can make a program dramatically faster. | | lvl:loop_control@L3#5 | level L3 way relation_to_neighbour: The initialization and the condition of a loop fix how many times it runs; one wrong bound makes it run once too many or too few. | | lvl:loop_control@L3#6 | level L3 way purpose_of_the_whole: Plan: counter-controlled loop - the loop variable is a stepper that walks a predictable sequence of values (0..N-1, 1..N, every 2nd value) and fixes the number of passes in advance. | | lvl:loop_control@L4#0 | level L4 way predict_a_change: Changing < to <= adds one pass; starting at 1 instead of 0 removes one; doubling the step halves the passes; reversing init and bound with i-- visits the same values in reverse order (and still processes the same set only if both ends are adjusted). | | lvl:loop_control@L4#1 | level L4 way diagnose_an_error: rule broken: The number of passes is fixed by the init, the test and the update together. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Wrong start value, < vs <=, a wrong step, or an extra update of the counter in the body (or outside the loop): the loop runs too few or too many passes (off by one, or skips values). | | lvl:loop_control@L4#2 | level L4 way transfer_to_a_new_program: Use explicit init/test/update control when the passes are counted or follow a fixed step; when the number of passes depends on data computed in the body, control the loop by that data (a while condition) instead. | | lvl:loop_control@L4#3 | level L4 way diagnose_an_error: rule broken: The update must move the loop variable toward making the condition false. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: An update in the wrong direction or a condition that the update cannot falsify (e.g. i > 3 with i++, or i != 10 with i += 3): infinite loop. | | lvl:loop_control@L4#4 | level L4 way diagnose_an_error: rule broken: Do not control a loop by an equality test on double values. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: for (double x = 0.0; x < 1.0; x += 0.1): after ten additions x is 0.9999999999999999, so the loop makes 11 passes instead of the intended 10. |

Edges offered: | edge | |---| | err:for_loop->BracelessMultiStatementBody | wrong rule: Indenting several statements under an if or for makes them all part of its body, even without braces. | right rule: Without braces only the first statement belongs to the if/for; the rest run once, after it. | | err:for_loop->ForCommaSeparators | wrong rule: Writes for (int i = 0, i < n, i++). | right rule: The three parts of a for header are separated by semicolons; commas only separate several statements inside the init or the update part. | | err:for_loop->SemicolonAfterIfHeader | wrong rule: if (x > 0); System.out.println("positive"); prints only for positive x. | right rule: The ; ends the if with an empty statement, so the next line always runs. | | err:for_loop->SemicolonAfterLoopHeader | wrong rule: Puts a ; right after for (...) or while (...). | right rule: A ; right after the loop header is a null (empty) loop body, so the statements written after it are not repeated by the loop. | | err:for_loop->WrongIterationCount | wrong rule: Updates the loop counter so that the loop runs the wrong number of times. | right rule: The init, test and update together decide the number of passes; trace them to check the count. | | mis:for_loop->DoubleLoopIndexCount | wrong rule: for (double x = 0.0; x <= 1.0; x += 0.1) runs exactly 11 times. | right rule: Using a double as a for-loop index is legal but bad practice: the number of iterations depends on an equality test between double values, which may not give the result you expect. | | mis:for_loop->FalseLoopRepeatsNextCode | wrong rule: A loop is an iterative if-else: while the condition is true the body repeats, and when it is false the code after the loop repeats. | right rule: Only the body is repeated; once the condition is false the code after the loop runs once. | | mis:for_loop->ForInitRepeats | wrong rule: The initialization of a for loop runs again after a pass of the body. | right rule: The initialization runs exactly once, before the first condition test. | | mis:for_loop->ForIsConditional | wrong rule: The body of a for statement executes at most once. | right rule: The body of a for statement runs once for every pass on which the condition is true, which can be many times. | | mis:for_loop->ForLoopPartSkipped | wrong rule: A pass of a loop may leave out one of its parts (the condition test, the body, the update, or the initialization). | right rule: Each pass of a for loop runs test, then body, then update, every time; the initialization runs once, at the start. | | mis:for_loop->ForUpdateBeforeBody | wrong rule: The update part of a for header (e.g. i = i - 4) runs before the body on each pass, so the first pass already sees the updated value. | right rule: The update runs after the body, before the next condition test; the first pass uses the initial value. | | mis:for_loop->ForWhileNotInterchangeable | wrong rule: Some loops can only be written with for, others only with while. | right rule: Any for loop can be rewritten as a while loop and vice versa; for just packages init, test and update. | | mis:for_loop->IdiomOverridesCode | wrong rule: An array loop processes the whole array from index 0 to length-1 and increments its index at the end of the body, whatever the code says. | right rule: The loop visits exactly the indices that its initialisation, guard and update produce, in the order in which its statements are written. | | mis:for_loop->LoopCountIsStatementCount | wrong rule: The repeat count of a counted loop says how many of the body statements are executed. | right rule: The repeat count is how many times the whole body runs; every pass runs all body statements. | | mis:for_loop->LoopHeaderIsEquations | wrong rule: The initialization, condition and update of a for header are equations that all hold at the same time. | right rule: The three header parts are statements run at different moments: init once, then condition test, body, update, repeated. | | mis:for_loop->LoopImpliedByOneTest | wrong rule: Testing one case is enough; Java will repeat the test for the other values by itself. | right rule: A statement runs once each time control reaches it; repeating a test for many values needs a loop. | | mis:for_loop->LoopStepAlwaysOne | wrong rule: A loop variable always goes up or down by 1, whatever the update says (so i = i - 4 is read as i--). | right rule: The loop variable changes exactly as the update expression says (i += 2, i = i - 4, i *= 2, ...). | | mis:for_loop->MissingBraces | wrong rule: Omits braces around a single-statement body of if, for or while. | right rule: Braces are optional for a single-statement body, but using them anyway avoids bugs when statements are added later. | | mis:for_loop->ProgramEndsAfterLoop | wrong rule: When a loop finishes the program ends, so code after the loop never runs. | right rule: When the loop condition becomes false, control continues with the first statement after the loop. | | mis:for_loop->ReturnDoesNotExitLoop | wrong rule: A return inside a loop does not end the loop; it sets a value each pass (the last one is returned) or returns several values. | right rule: When return executes, the method ends at once, so the loop stops on that pass. | | mis:for_loop->SingleIterationInsteadOfLoop | wrong rule: A task that must be repeated is written once, without a loop, as if one pass were enough. | right rule: A step that must happen several times (or an unknown number of times) needs a loop such as while or for; code without a loop runs once. |

Edges offered: | edge | |---| | mis:loop_variable->BodyChangeIgnoredByCondition | wrong rule: Changing the loop variable inside the body does not affect the loop condition; the loop still runs its planned number of times. | right rule: The condition is tested with the current value of the variable, including changes made in the body. | | mis:loop_variable->DoubleLoopIndexCount | wrong rule: for (double x = 0.0; x <= 1.0; x += 0.1) runs exactly 11 times. | right rule: Using a double as a for-loop index is legal but bad practice: the number of iterations depends on an equality test between double values, which may not give the result you expect. | | mis:loop_variable->ForInitRepeats | wrong rule: The initialization of a for loop runs again after a pass of the body. | right rule: The initialization runs exactly once, before the first condition test. | | mis:loop_variable->LoopOutputSameEachPass | wrong rule: A loop prints the same thing on every pass; the changing loop variable does not affect what the body does. | right rule: The body uses the current value of the loop variable, so its output can differ on each pass. | | mis:loop_variable->LoopUpdateChangesDirection | wrong rule: The update of the loop variable can change from pass to pass (e.g. switch direction) although the code is the same. | right rule: The update expression is the same on every pass; the loop variable changes by the rule written in the update. | | mis:loop_variable->LoopVariableLifetimeScope | wrong rule: The for variable i is a new variable on every pass rather than one variable changed by the update. | right rule: The for variable i is created once by the init, and the update changes that same variable on every pass. | | mis:loop_variable->LoopVariableLimitsValues | wrong rule: The range of the loop variable limits the values that can be read or printed inside the loop. | right rule: The loop variable only counts passes; other values read or printed in the body are not bounded by it. |
